gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: If we had left earlier, we ___ the ferry.
gaps.hint: unreal past, would have plus participle
gaps.explanation: Third conditionals take 'would have' plus the past participle in the result clause: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: If you order before midnight, delivery ___ nothing.
gaps.hint: result clause of a first conditional
gaps.explanation: The result of a real future condition takes 'will': will cost.

gaps.sentence: You'd have got a better exchange rate ___ at the bank instead of the airport.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes 'if + past perfect'.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ here now, she would know exactly what to do.
gaps.hint: unreal present needs the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: For unreal present conditions, formal English uses 'were' for all persons: were.

gaps.sentence: If the temperature ___ below freezing tonight, the race will be postponed.
gaps.explanation: First conditional: present simple in the if-clause, will + infinitive in the result.
